strings: On Darkshore's coast, Gelkak Gyromast needs help restoring his mechanical first mate. His winding key shattered on the rocks, and wildlife and murlocs scavenged the three pieces. Recovering them is the first step toward setting his crew right.

Gelkak Gyromast is a gnome pirate stranded on Darkshore, far from the South Seas. He says aggressive threshadons attacked and sank his vessel just off the coast. The wreck cast him ashore among the flotsam, marooned and separated from his crew.

Gelkak's first concern is his first mate, not provisions or gold. The companion needs a specialized key to operate, but the key shattered into three pieces when Gelkak crashed on the rocky shoals. Before he could gather them, reef crawlers on the beach, foreststriders near the woods, and scavengers from the Greymist murloc tribe carried the shiny pieces away.
Gelkak speaks of his first mate with a sea captain's fierce loyalty. He says the companion needs to be put in working order, and the broken key is vital to winding it up again.
Gelkak Gyromast is a gnome pirate whose vessel was attacked and sunk by predatory threshadons off Darkshore.
gelkak gyromast | who is the gnome pirate | darkshore gnome pirate
What is the key used for?
The key is needed to reactivate and wind up Gelkak's mechanical first mate, which shut down during the shipwreck.
why does gelkak need the key | gelkak key purpose | first mate key
Where did the three pieces of the key go?
The top piece went to foreststriders, the middle piece to Greymist murlocs, and the bottom piece to coastal reef crawlers after the key broke on shore.
where are the key pieces | who stole the key | broken key darkshore
Why was a gnome pirate sailing near Darkshore?
Gelkak was sailing off northern Kalimdor in search of plunder when hostile threshadons ended his voyage.
why is gelkak in darkshore | pirates in darkshore
What happens after the key is reassembled?
With all three pieces of his key, Gelkak can wind up his companion and continue with Gyromast's Revenge.
what next after key | gyromast retrieval follow up
Who are the murlocs holding the key piece?
Greymist murlocs scavenged the middle piece. Their tribe lives among wreckage from drowned ships along Darkshore's shoals.
darkshore murlocs | greymist murloc key | shipwreck murlocs

As an engineer, you can appreciate the challenge of keeping clockwork contraptions working after a violent shipwreck in saltwater.
As a gnome, you may recognize Gelkak's reliance on clockwork devices instead of flesh-and-blood shipmates, though his pirate life is unusual among your kin.
Why does Gelkak Gyromast want his key restored?

Gelkak Gyromast was shipwrecked off the coast of Darkshore when threshadons sank his vessel. Left stranded and surrounded by hostile wildlife, he desperately needs his mechanical first mate back in working order to defend himself and enact his revenge against the creatures that wrecked his voyage. Without the three shattered pieces of the winding key, his clockwork companion remains entirely inert.
why gelkak wants key | gelkak gyromast motive | why help gelkak
Why does Gelkak Gyromast need your help?

Gelkak is a marooned pirate with no crew left beside him and no friends among the local night elves. Having barely survived his ship sinking and washing ashore battered on the beach, he is in no shape to battle the vicious reef crawlers, foreststriders, and murlocs that made off with his broken key shards.

In Northshire Valley, recruits strike at kobolds in Echo Ridge Mine. Marshal McBride ordered the attack after scouts found the mine overrun.

Marshal McBride sends recruits against the kobolds in Echo Ridge Mine. Scouts found the mine overrun, and the garrison fears the creatures will strengthen their hold if left alone. The kobolds dig through the tunnels, gather stolen resources, and multiply. Recruits must thin their numbers to protect Northshire Valley, with its farms and spiritual retreat.

New recruits are sent into the mine because the Stormwind Army is stretched thin. Garrison forces guard the southern borders, while unrest is rumored across Elwynn. Officers like McBride must call on willing hands. A recruit who proves reliable at Echo Ridge earns the army’s respect and is ready for more difficult work elsewhere in the kingdom.
Why are kobolds infesting the Echo Ridge Mine?

Kobolds are drawn to mineral-rich tunnels and abandoned quarries. With Stormwind’s forces stretched thin, they can enter unguarded places like Echo Ridge to dig burrows, hoard gold, and claim underground shelter.
why kobolds in mine | echo ridge kobolds | what are kobolds doing
Marshal McBride orders the skirmish. He commands the Stormwind Army forces at Northshire Abbey and oversees the valley’s defense with limited manpower.
who gives skirmish quest | marshal mcbride orders
What is the strategic importance of Echo Ridge Mine?
Echo Ridge Mine holds stone and ore needed to maintain Northshire and help rebuild Stormwind. Kobolds on Northshire’s northern border threaten the abbey and nearby vineyards.
why echo ridge matters | echo ridge mine importance
Where does this mission lead next?
After the first kobold laborers are cleared from the mine, Marshal McBride sends you toward Goldshire to aid the region’s defense.
what quest after skirmish | next step after echo ridge
Why doesn't the Stormwind Army clear the mine themselves?

Stormwind’s forces are short on soldiers, defending distant borders and answering bandit attacks across Elwynn. McBride relies on new recruits for local threats while seasoned guards hold defensive lines.
why recruits | where are stormwind soldiers
Are kobolds intelligent enough to be an organized military threat?
Kobold laborers are cowardly and simple-minded alone, but territorial and aggressive in numbers. Left unchecked, they dig winding tunnels, set traps in caverns, and draw larger, better-armed vermin.
are kobolds smart | kobold danger level

As a warrior, you face swarming kobold workers in close quarters, among the first entrenched foes you meet.
As an Alliance member, you help reclaim mines that hold stone and ore for rebuilding and fortifying human settlements after the war.
As a miner, you help make it possible to safely dig and smelt valuable mineral veins across Northshire Valley.
As a human, clearing Echo Ridge is your first true test of arms in defense of your ancestral kingdom. You prove your mettle to Stormwind’s officers.
Why does Marshal McBride want the kobolds in Echo Ridge Mine culled?

Marshal McBride knows that the longer the kobolds remain unchallenged in Echo Ridge Mine, the deeper their foothold in Northshire becomes. Leaving them unmolested invites them to entrench themselves further and threaten the valley, making their eventual removal far bloodier and risking the security of Northshire Abbey itself.

Corporal Kaleb's mechanical cooking pot, bought off a goblin trader in Booty Bay, was a marvel until it broke. Kaleb asks you to take it back to the goblin Krazek for mending.

Corporal Kaleb does most of the cooking for the camp. It used to be heavy work until Kaleb bought a mechanical pot off a goblin trader in Booty Bay, and the pot spared Kaleb hour after hour. Then it broke. Krazek's Crock Pot must go back to the goblin Krazek to be fixed, and Kaleb hopes you will carry it there.

Krazek calls the pot ingenious work, though prone to popping a spring or slipping a gear from time to time. Looking it over, Krazek finds the steam charger rusted out, the knuckle-gasket cracked and the fobulator missing teeth. Krazek can mend it, but a price comes with it, as it always does.
Corporal Kaleb, on whom the camp's cooking mostly falls, sends you. The mechanical pot Kaleb bought has broken down.
who gives krazek's cookery | who starts krazek cookery | corporal kaleb quest
Krazek is the goblin trader of Booty Bay who sold the pot to Kaleb.
where is krazek | krazek location | krazek booty bay

A mechanical cooking pot named Krazek's Crock Pot, which broke after sparing Kaleb a great deal of work.
what is krazek's crock pot | what do i bring krazek
Why did Kaleb buy a cooking pot from Krazek?
Kaleb handles most of the camp's cooking, and the pot spared Kaleb a great many hours until it broke.

Corruption is spreading through Darkshore, where Tharnariun Treetender hopes to save the afflicted wildlife. He asks travelers to calm a rabid thistle bear with an enchanted relic and bring it back alive.

A creeping sickness twists Darkshore’s beasts into maddened, aggressive versions of themselves. Thistle bears suffer most, their rabid frenzy threatening travelers and the coast’s fragile balance. Night elf sentinels often answer with steel, while druids seek to understand the sickness and heal its cause.

Tharnariun Treetender refuses to kill the corrupted beasts without first trying to save them. He made a trap called Tharnariun’s Hope. Set on the forest floor, its soothing light briefly calms a raging thistle bear. Pacified, the bear follows the traveler back to Tharnariun’s outpost for study.

When an infected bear reaches camp, Tharnariun tries to purge its sickness with restorative magic. His first attempt ends in disaster: cleansing energies overwhelm the weakened animal, and it collapses and dies. The failure shows how deeply the dark plague has taken hold.
Who gives the quest Plagued Lands?
Tharnariun Treetender, a night elf druid in Auberdine, gives this task. He seeks a cure for Darkshore’s afflicted wildlife.
quest giver plagued lands | tharnariun darkshore quest | who starts plagued lands
What is the objective of Plagued Lands?
Use Tharnariun’s Hope to trap and calm a Rabid Thistle Bear in Darkshore, then lead it back to Tharnariun alive.
plagued lands goal | what to do in plagued lands | how to catch bear darkshore
What happens to the bear when you bring it back?
Tharnariun tries to cleanse the bear with healing magic, but the sickness has advanced too far. The strain overwhelms it, and it dies after the treatment.

Why are the thistle bears rabid?
A creeping plague is spreading through Darkshore, poisoning local wildlife and driving the thistle bears into mindless aggression.
why are bears sick in darkshore | darkshore plague bears | darkshore corruption

As a druid, you share Tharnariun’s grief as nature falls to corruption. The bear’s tragic loss shows how deeply the disease has spread through the land.
As an Alliance traveler crossing northern Kalimdor, you face untamed corruption pressing against the borders of settled lands.
As a night elf, seeing Darkshore’s native flora and fauna decay into rabid madness is an affront to Cenarius and the balance of nature you are sworn to protect.
Why does Tharnariun Treetender want you to capture a rabid thistle bear?

A dark sickness spreads through Darkshore, gripping the minds and bodies of the local wildlife. The thistle bears have suffered the worst of it, turning from noble woodland beasts into frenzied engines of destruction. Tharnariun Treetender believes he may have devised a cure for the affliction, but he needs a living, rabid subject brought directly to him so he can test his remedy and halt the corruption before it claims all the forest's creatures.
why capture thistle bear | tharnariun motive plagued lands | why does tharnariun want a bear
What are rabid thistle bears and why are you targeting them?

Thistle bears are native forest predators of Darkshore, typically revered as stalwart and noble beasts. However, an unnatural contagion has recently infected their ranks, driving them into a mad frenzy and warping their minds. You are sent after them not to slaughter them outright, but to lure and pacify a sick specimen with Tharnariun's trap so it can be safely examined in hopes of developing an antidote.
what are rabid thistle bears | why target rabid thistle bears | rabid thistle bear darkshore

Gelriz has been muscling out the moguls appointed by the trade princes and now makes a move on the most notorious pirate of all, and Baron Revilgaz will not stand for it. In response, Kebok in Booty Bay directs adventurers to steal strange blue crystals that Venture Company geologists have been finding near Lake Nazferiti.

Gelriz has stepped over the line by shoving aside moguls chosen by the trade princes and making a move on the most notorious pirate of all. Baron Revilgaz refuses to permit such insolence, instructing Kebok to handle the intrusion however he sees fit. Kebok's chosen response is outright theft, targeting the strange blue stones that Venture Company mining crews have been unearthing.

Venture Company geologists operating around Lake Nazferiti have taken a keen interest in these unusual crystals. Kebok wants eight samples brought back to Booty Bay, unconcerned with how they are acquired so long as they end up in his hands.

Examining the returned specimens reveals that they have undergone a tumbling process, suggesting the Venture Company intends to utilize them as fuel or an industrial catalyst. Kebok intends to dispatch samples to Head Chemist Gigglefont for more detailed study.
Who gives the quest Hostile Takeover?
Kebok, operating out of the pirate haven of Booty Bay in Stranglethorn Vale, gives this assignment on behalf of Baron Revilgaz.

Gelriz pushed aside moguls who had been appointed by the trade princes and has now made a move on the most notorious pirate, which Revilgaz will not tolerate.

The crystals are carried by Venture Company geologists working around Lake Nazferiti.

In Darkshore, Tharnariun Treetender faces a hard choice over the infected thistle bears. His attempt to cure one has failed, and he asks you to kill the rabid beasts before they harm other creatures or spread the sickness.

Tharnariun Treetender has searched for a remedy to the sickness spreading through Darkshore's wildlife. He tried to cleanse a captured bear, but the thistle bears remain diseased and violent. Now he asks you to put them down. He fears they will maul other creatures and carry the sickness farther into the ancient woodlands.

Tharnariun asks you to kill twenty rabid bears, though he knows it will not cure the plague. The killings buy time for Auberdine's defenders. Until anyone finds and severs the source of the forest's corruption, the settlement has no other way to hold back the aggressive herds and the danger they bring.
Why does Tharnariun want the thistle bears killed instead of cured?
Tharnariun tried to cleanse a captured bear, but the cure failed and the beast died. Now the diseased bears threaten other creatures, so killing them is his last resort to slow the sickness's spread.
why kill the bears | why not cure bears | tharnariun bear quest
Tharnariun is a night elf caretaker in Auberdine. He studies the ailments affecting Darkshore's plants and animals and works to preserve nature's balance against the spreading corruption.
tharnariun role | who gives cleansing of the infected
Does slaying the rabid bears actually end the plague?
No. Tharnariun warns that killing the rabid bears will not stop the plague. It buys the forest and Auberdine's residents time by slowing the spread of infection and violence.
does this fix darkshore | is the plague cured

After you report back, Tharnariun asks you to prepare for more bloodshed and offers Tharnariun's Hope, which continues the effort to deal with the blighted wildlife.
next quest after cleansing | what follows cleasning infected

rabid thistle bear location | where are bears darkshore
What caused the thistle bears to go rabid?
A mysterious taint sweeping through northern Kalimdor's woodlands has corrupted the bears, turning peaceful wildlife into frenzied, aggressive beasts that Tharnariun's attempted cure cannot heal.

As a druid, you may find Tharnariun's command especially painful. It is an act of mercy and care for the forest, not ordinary hunting.
As a hunter, you know that culling diseased predators can protect the wider ecology, even when the cause remains unknown.
As a kaldorei, you bear the weight of ordering corrupted beasts killed. The sickness has reached deep into your ancestral homeland since the war.
What are rabid thistle bears and why must they be killed?

Thistle bears are native forest predators that usually live in harmony with the wildlands of Darkshore. However, a creeping, unnatural plague spreading through the woods has driven many of them rabid and violently deranged. In their tainted madness, these diseased beasts attack other wildlife, menace travelers near Auberdine, and ravage the woodland ecology. Because attempts to cure their affliction have failed, putting them down is the only way to contain the devastation.
rabid thistle bears | who are rabid thistle bears | why kill rabid thistle bears

In Darkshore, Tharnariun Treetender's work against the wildlife sickness reaches a grim turning point. After travelers put down infected beasts across the woodlands, he sends an Alliance champion after the rabid Den Mother northeast of Auberdine.

After the Third War, an unnatural rabid sickness began afflicting Darkshore's wild creatures. Tharnariun Treetender, stationed in Auberdine, spent days asking travelers to put down infected beasts and ease the forest's suffering. But killing rabid thistle bears treated only a symptom. Tharnariun decided the source among the local bears had to be removed: their matriarch, the Den Mother.

Northeast of Auberdine, near the ancient ruins of Bashal'Aran, the Den Mother lurks in a cavern. She was once a vital guardian of the woodland fauna. The affliction spreading across northern Kalimdor consumed her, and she kept bearing and raising litters of rabid cubs. Alliance heroes hunted down the matriarch in her den, ending her torment and stemming the tide of frenzied bears prowling the coastal highway.

After the Den Mother's death, Tharnariun offers profound thanks, though melancholy shadows his words. For the kaldorei, raising weapons against woodland creatures is agonizing. Dark forces press against their new home, and many despair or seek shelter. The defenders of Auberdine accept the heavy moral burden of protecting their wilderness.

Tharnariun Treetender is a night elf caretaker stationed in Auberdine. Distraught by the blight and madness warping Darkshore's wildlife, he oversees efforts to study and track the suffering animals, then put them out of their misery.
tharnariun | who gives tharnariun's hope | treetender auberdine
Where is the Den Mother located?
The Den Mother dwells in a cave in the hills northeast of Auberdine, just east of the ruins of Bashal'Aran.
where is den mother | den mother cave location | find den mother
Why must the Den Mother be killed instead of cured?

The affliction ravaging Darkshore's wildlife grips the beasts and drives them into violent frenzies. With no immediate cure, and the Den Mother raising rabid offspring, Tharnariun decided that killing her was the only way to stop the sickness from spreading further.
can den mother be saved | why kill den mother | cure den mother
What quests lead up to Tharnariun's Hope?
The chain has three parts. It begins with 'Plagued Lands', continues through 'Cleansing of the Infected', and ends with 'Tharnariun's Hope'.
prerequisites for tharnariuns hope | quest chain tharnariun
What is making the animals of Darkshore sick?
Tharnariun names no source. He knows only that a sickness is spreading across Darkshore, gripping the minds and bodies of those it touches, and that thistle bears have been hit hardest.
why are bears rabid in darkshore | darkshore animal plague cause | what corrupted the bears
Why does Tharnariun mention people escaping to fortified lands?

Auberdine is an exposed coastal outpost beset by ghosts, corrupted wildlife, and hostile creatures. As night elf civilization struggles to rebuild after the Burning Legion's invasion, some residents feel overwhelmed and hide or retreat toward safer Alliance bastions.
auberdine | bashal'aran | cleansing of the infected | darkshore | den mother | rabid thistle bear | tharnariun treetender | tharnariun's hope
As a druid, you hold bears in high spiritual esteem through the teachings of Ursoc. Killing a corrupted Den Mother reminds you solemnly of nature's delicate balance and the tragedies of corruption.
As a hunter, you understand the tragedy of an apex predator driven mad by disease. You know that culling an infected beast can be the truest act of mercy.
As an Alliance member, you help protect Auberdine and strengthen the Alliance's foothold along northern Kalimdor's coast, defending night elf lands from growing wilderness threats.
For night elves, slaying woodland beasts, especially a matriarch bear, violates their deep reverence for nature. This duty is bitter and sorrowful.

The Den Mother is a massive, corrupted bear laired in a cave northeast near the ruins of Bashal'Aran. She is the source giving birth to or harboring the rabid thistle bears that plague the region. Slaying her cuts off the influx of diseased beasts menacing Auberdine.

Red Silk Bandanas is a mission issued by Scout Riell on behalf of the People's Militia. It directs Alliance adventurers into the Deadmines to hunt down high-ranking Defias operatives and bring back their distinctive red silk masks as proof.

While common cutpurses and highwaymen throughout Westfall tie coarse red cloth around their faces, the Defias Brotherhood maintains a strict internal hierarchy indicated by fabric. Scout Riell and the People's Militia have discovered that rank-and-file bandits wear rough weave, while senior conspirators and inner-circle operatives are distinguished by fine red silk. Stripping these bandanas directly targets the experienced officers coordinating Edwin VanCleef's uprising.

Because silk marks seniority, the greatest concentration of these high-ranking outlaws gathers deep within the Deadmines beneath Moonbrook. Sentinels and scouts stationed outside Sentinel Hill rely on freelance champions to push into the contested subterranean tunnels. Every silk bandana recovered represents one less lieutenant organizing ambushes, defending weapon caches, or enforcing VanCleef's rule across Westfall.
Why do the Defias wear red bandanas?

The red bandana serves as the unified emblem and calling card of the Defias Brotherhood across Stormwind's territories. It conceals their identities while signaling allegiance to Edwin VanCleef's rebellious movement.
defias mask meaning | why red masks | defias uniform
What makes the red silk bandanas special compared to regular bandanas?
According to Scout Riell, the fabric denotes status within the Brotherhood. Common street thugs wear coarse, cheap material, while veterans, officers, and trusted lieutenants are awarded red silk.
why red silk | silk vs cloth defias | silk bandana difference
Scout Riell is an operative serving the People's Militia in Westfall, tasked with tracking Defias movements and directing adventurers to strike at their strongholds around the Deadmines.
scout riell westfall | who gives red silk bandanas quest
Where are the Defias wearing silk bandanas located?

The militia knows that silk bandanas denote high-ranking officers rather than mere thugs. By eliminating these key figures and demanding their bandanas as proof, Riell hopes to shatter the brotherhood's command structure and finally reclaim Westfall for its people.

You are hunting the elite officers and veterans of the Defias Brotherhood stationed in and around Edwin VanCleef's stronghold within the Deadmines. Unlike the rough cutthroats roaming Westfall's farmsteads, these high-ranking members guard the brotherhood's base of operations, oversee the hidden works deep beneath Moonbrook, and direct the syndicate's operations across the region.
who are we hunting | red silk bandana target | who drops silk bandanas
Why does Scout Riell ask you instead of the Stormwind guards?

Stormwind has virtually abandoned Westfall, offering little to no military support while the House of Nobles ignores the growing crisis. The local People's Militia is stretched thin, lacking the numbers, training, and resources to mount a frontal assault against fortified criminal bastions. Riell and her fellow scouts must rely on capable adventurers to infiltrate the treacherous Deadmines and confront the brotherhood's leadership directly.

After being rescued from an ambush in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Private Thorsen explains why he re-enlisted with Kurzen's men. He directs you back to the Rebel Camp so his commander can verify his covert intentions.

Following his rescue, Private Thorsen admits the scene looks bad and asks to explain. He claims Lieutenant Doren ordered him to re-enlist with Colonel Kurzen's men to gather desperately needed intelligence for the rebellion. What seemed to be an opportunity to infiltrate Kurzen's Compound quickly turned disastrous, forcing Thorsen to refer you directly to Doren at the Rebel Camp for official confirmation while begging for complete discretion.

Lieutenant Doren confirms that Thorsen was indeed acting under his orders. The rebels were once fiercely loyal to Kurzen until Kurzen's corruption twisted their loyalty into rage, and discovery of Thorsen's dealings would prompt his own comrades to slit his throat. Because only Doren, Sergeant Yohwa, and Thorsen were supposed to know of the plan, the failed ambush indicates an unsettling truth: an unknown traitor lurks within their ranks.
Why was Private Thorsen meeting with Kurzen's forces?
He was acting under orders from Lieutenant Doren to re-enlist among Colonel Kurzen's men as a spy and gather vital military intelligence for the rebels.

Rest and Relaxation is an introductory Alliance quest directing newly trained adventurers from Northshire south along the road to the Lion's Pride Inn. Run by Innkeeper Farley, the bustling Goldshire tavern offers food, drink, and a warm hearth for those seeking a reprieve from the road.

After cutting their teeth in Northshire, weary travelers are pointed south toward the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. The road south leads directly to the beloved tavern, run by Innkeeper Farley. For new adventurers stepping out into the wider forest, it represents the first major outpost offering hearth, shelter, and hot meals away from the Abbey.

Innkeeper Farley takes pride in his establishment's hospitality, operating under the motto of providing rest and relaxation for the tired and cold. Adventurers who mention their referral can take advantage of Farley's good graces, settling by the open fire to enjoy a warm meal, sturdy ale, and a much-needed respite before journeying further into Elwynn.
Where can I find the Lion's Pride Inn?
The Lion's Pride Inn is located south along the main road leading out of Northshire Valley, situated at the heart of the town of Goldshire. Travelers heading south cannot miss the welcoming tavern.
where is lions pride inn | how to get to lion's pride inn | find lions pride
Innkeeper Farley is the hospitable proprietor of the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. A close friend of local contacts in Northshire, he welcomes weary adventurers with food, drink, and a warm hearth.

Rest and Relaxation directs novice adventurers leaving Northshire toward Goldshire's central hub, introducing them to the services, refreshments, and lodgings offered by Innkeeper Farley at the Lion's Pride Inn.

The Trial of the Sea Lion is a sacred rite undertaken by druids in Moonglade on their journey to master Aquatic Form. Initiates are tasked with recovering two scattered pendant halves that embody the sea lion's agility and endurance, then uniting them at the Shrine of Remulos. By forging the complete Pendant of the Sea Lion, the druid proves their harmony with the water and prepares to channel the creature's spirit.

To gain the ability to navigate Azeroth's deep waters, druid initiates must undertake tests of attunement in the sacred glade of Moonglade. The Trial of the Sea Lion represents the second of these essential rites, following earlier preparations in their spiritual training. Supervised by Dendrite Starblaze in the village of Nighthaven, the trial challenges druids to comprehend how two distinct traits—graceful speed and resilient stamina—must exist in balance. Without grasping both dimensions of the sea lion's nature, an initiate cannot hope to harness its form or withstand the perils of the ocean depths.

The physical and spiritual heart of the trial requires reassembling the Pendant of the Sea Lion from two severed halves. One half channels the agility of the sea lion aspect, reflecting its capacity to glide effortlessly through turbulent currents. The other half draws upon the creature's boundless endurance, representing the fortitude needed to dive long into freezing water without faltering. Initiates must consult the inhabitants of Moonglade for clues to uncover these dispersed relics across the world, demonstrating both their resourcefulness and their willingness to seek guidance within their sacred sanctuary.

Once both relics are secured, the initiate must bring the pieces into proximity with the Shrine of Remulos to bind them back into a single talisman. The Keeper's sanctum provides the tranquil, potent energies necessary to meld the disparate powers of agility and endurance into harmony. Presenting the restored Pendant of the Sea Lion to Dendrite Starblaze in Nighthaven seals the completion of the trial.
